body:
Part of #2574 (research answers 3, 4 and 6).

Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words (quoted in #2574):
> "Maybe even the camproj file so we can run it as a verification of sorts."

## Scope
- Define the sim job file as serde data in `camcraft-sim` (`app` already depends on it): stock, fixtures, the tool geometry for each `T`, the work offset values, the model facets or a model path, and the expected toolpath (CL) for each section.
- `app`: write the job for one setup of a project. CLI verb `camcraft-cli sim-job <file.camproj> [--setup N] -o <job.json>` and the MCP tool `export_sim_job` (same function).
- `camcraft-sim`: `--job <job.json>`. With a `.camproj` argument, it runs `camcraft-cli sim-job` from its own folder. If `camcraft-cli` is missing, it refuses by name.
- New check "compare": parse the G-code back and compare it move by move with the expected toolpath, inside a stated tolerance. Each difference gives its NC line and the operation name. This is the round trip that #2213 question 6 names.
- With a job, the gouge check runs against the model.

## Done means
Tests in `crates/app/tests/` pin the job export for a project with stock, fixtures and two tools, and the MCP tool. Tests in `crates/simview/tests/` pin the compare check (a clean round trip of a `fanuc.cps` program passes; an edited line fails with its line number) and the refusal when `camcraft-cli` is missing.

Depends on #2586.
